title: A 2D light uses PCF13 shadows
evidence: Light2D.shadow_filter is 2 (PCF13). The 2D lights page says PCF13 is the softest and the most expensive, and should be used on only a few lights. PCF5 is 1 and None is 0.
expected_effect: A cheaper 2D shadow filter than the one the page calls the most demanding.

title: Several 2D lights cast shadows
heuristic_rationale: Four shadow-casting Light2D nodes is a review cut. The 2D lights page says even PCF13 should be limited to a few lights.
evidence: At least four Light2D nodes have shadow_enabled.
suggestion: Disable shadow_enabled on fill lights. Leave shadows on the one or two lights that define the silhouette.

title: 2D HDR is enabled
evidence: rendering/viewport/hdr_2d is true. The default is false.
suggestion: Turn hdr_2d off unless 2D glow or HDR canvases need values above 1.
tradeoff: 2D buffers go back to the low-dynamic-range format. Bright 2D glow can clip.
expected_effect: A narrower 2D framebuffer. Measure canvas time if 2D is the scene.

title: 2D SDF oversize is above the default
evidence: sdf/oversize index is 2 or 3. The hint is 100%, 120%, 150%, 200%. The default index is 1 (120%). A 2D light is in the scene.
tradeoff: The signed-distance field covers less margin around the viewport.

title: 2D SDF scale is at full resolution
evidence: sdf/scale index is 0. The hint is 100%, 50%, 25%. The default index is 1 (50%). Shadow-casting 2D lights are present.
suggestion: The default 50% scale is the cheaper SDF. Index 0 is the sharper, heavier field. Set it back to 1 if you did not choose 100% on purpose.
expected_effect: A quarter of the SDF pixels versus 100%, because the scale is per axis.

title: 2D item buffer is above the default while canvas draws are high
heuristic_rationale: item_buffer_size defaults to 16384. The rule flags it only when it is larger than that and canvas draw calls exceed 1000. 1000 is a review cut, not a batching budget.
evidence: item_buffer_size is above 16384 and the canvas viewport draw-call counter is above 1000.
suggestion: Lower item_buffer_size toward 16384 after confirming the 2D scene still batches. uniform_set_cache_size defaults to 4096.
tradeoff: A buffer that is too small splits batches.
expected_effect: Less reserved 2D batch memory if the extra size is unused.

title: Canvas draw calls are high
heuristic_rationale: 2000 canvas draw calls is a review cut so a 2D frame with a large VIEWPORT_CANVAS_DRAW_CALLS count is surfaced. Godot does not publish that number as a limit.
evidence: Viewport canvas draw calls are above 2000.
suggestion: Reuse textures and materials so CanvasItem batching can merge items. The GPU optimization page explains draw calls as the CPU-side submission cost.
tradeoff: Merging atlases changes how art is packed.
expected_effect: Fewer canvas draws. Read the counter again with collect_metrics.

title: A TileMapLayer places many scene tiles
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: An enabled TileMapLayer places more than 256 cells from a TileSetScenesCollectionSource (bounded to 4096 inspected cells per scan). The 256 cutoff is a review heuristic shared with the other TileMap checks. Godot docs: "Scene tiles come with a greater performance overhead compared to atlases, as every scene is instanced individually for every placed tile."
suggestion: Use atlas tiles for static decoration and keep scene tiles for cells that need their own nodes (scripts, collision behaviour, lights).
tradeoff: Atlas tiles cannot carry per-cell scripts or child nodes.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Capture a visual reference; change one feature and repeat frame timing plus relevant CPU or GPU profiling in the same scene on target hardware.

title: A TileMapLayer creates many per-cell light occluders
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: An enabled, locally visible TileMapLayer with occlusion_enabled has more than 256 inspected atlas-cell occluder polygons on layers with nonzero light masks or SDF collision enabled. Closed polygons require at least three points; open polygons require two. The native path creates a separate occluder for each cell/layer/polygon. This object-count cutoff is a review heuristic, not proof of active shadow or SDF cost. Runtime tile-data overrides and invalid references are skipped; cell and resource limits are reported.
suggestion: Compare consolidated static occluder outlines, or disable tile occlusion where neither 2D shadows nor SDF collision need it. Measure canvas CPU/GPU time while moving lights and editing tiles.
tradeoff: Changing outlines or disabling occlusion changes 2D shadows and SDF-based effects or particle collision. Preserve holes, light masks, moving tiles and dynamic updates.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Capture a visual reference; change one feature and repeat frame timing plus relevant CPU or GPU profiling in the same scene on target hardware.

title: Animated tiles record many canvas animation slices
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: An enabled, locally visible TileMapLayer has more than 4096 authored animation frames summed across inspected texture-assigned atlas cells with more than one frame. The native draw path records an animation slice and texture-region command for every authored frame, plus a reset slice. This counts configured command construction, not simultaneous GPU draws; inactive slices do not draw every frame. The threshold is a measurement heuristic. Runtime tile-data overrides and uninspected cells are not inferred.
suggestion: Compare fewer authored animation frames or fewer animated background cells, measuring both canvas frame time and tile-edit/rebuild spikes along the same camera route.
tradeoff: Fewer frames reduce animation smoothness; static replacements remove motion. Lowering playback speed alone does not reduce the recorded frame commands.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Capture a visual reference; change one feature and repeat frame timing plus relevant CPU or GPU profiling in the same scene on target hardware.

title: A populated TileMapLayer uses small rendering quadrants
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: An enabled, locally visible TileMapLayer without Y sorting has rendering_quadrant_size at most 4 and more than 256 inspected atlas cells with assigned textures. Native rendering groups cells into quadrants, then canvas items. The cutoff is a measurement heuristic; tile count is not draw-call count. Scene-collection cells, invalid references and runtime tile-data overrides are skipped. At most 4096 cells per scene scan and 32 data layers and 32 collision/occlusion polygons per layer per tile are inspected; omissions are reported.
suggestion: Compare the default rendering quadrant size of 16, profiling canvas work along the same camera route and during tile edits.
tradeoff: Larger quadrants reduce culling/update granularity and may rebuild more content after an edit. Retain small quadrants where measurements favor them.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Capture a visual reference; change one feature and repeat frame timing plus relevant CPU or GPU profiling in the same scene on target hardware.

title: A Y-sorted TileMapLayer creates many rendering groups
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: An enabled, locally visible TileMapLayer uses Y sorting with more than 256 inspected texture-assigned atlas cells across more than 64 Y-position buckets. Buckets follow the checked native formula: int((map_to_local(cell).y + tile y_sort_origin + layer y_sort_origin) * 100). Y sorting uses these groups instead of rendering_quadrant_size. Group count does not prove visible draw calls or cost. Runtime tile-data overrides are skipped and scan omissions are reported.
suggestion: Compare separating flat floor/background tiles into a layer without Y sorting while keeping overlap-sensitive tiles on the sorted layer.
tradeoff: Disabling sorting can break character/prop overlap and visual order. Preserve per-tile origins and verify movement through the scene.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Capture a visual reference; change one feature and repeat frame timing plus relevant CPU or GPU profiling in the same scene on target hardware.

title: A rounded Line2D exceeds the default arc precision
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: A visible Line2D has positive width, enough points for its rounded joints or enabled open caps, and round_precision above eight. LineBuilder uses this value to subdivide arcs into triangles. The threshold is the documented default, not a hardware budget.
suggestion: Compare the default precision on rounded lines, especially lines rebuilt frequently or displayed small.
tradeoff: Corners and end caps can look more faceted; retain detail for large on-screen curves.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Capture a visual reference; change one feature and repeat frame timing plus relevant CPU or GPU profiling in the same scene on target hardware.

title: A 3D sprite or label requests an opaque alpha prepass
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: SpriteBase3D or Label3D uses ALPHA_CUT_OPAQUE_PREPASS without a material override. Both class references describe this mode as slower than alpha blending or discard because it first draws fully opaque pixels in the depth prepass.
suggestion: Compare alpha discard where hard cutouts are acceptable, or alpha blending where overlap sorting remains correct.
tradeoff: Discard can harm antialiased text and translucent edges; blending can introduce sorting errors. Keep the prepass when correct appearance needs it.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Capture a visual reference; change one feature and repeat frame timing plus relevant CPU or GPU profiling in the same scene on target hardware.

title: A BackBufferCopy copies the entire viewport
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: A visible BackBufferCopy uses viewport mode or rectangle mode with an exactly empty Rect2, which the native renderer also treats as a full copy. The copied pixel count scales with viewport size.
suggestion: Compare a tight nonempty copy rectangle that contains all screen-texture samples needed by the following effects, or disable an unused copy.
tradeoff: Sampling outside the copied region produces undefined or stale content; camera movement and effect offsets must fit the region.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Capture a visual reference; change one feature and repeat frame timing plus relevant CPU or GPU profiling in the same scene on target hardware.

title: HDR output turns on HDR 2D
evidence: Godot prints "HDR 2D was automatically enabled because HDR output was requested in project settings." when display/window/hdr/request_hdr_output is on and rendering/viewport/hdr_2d is off. The root viewport then renders 2D in HDR anyway, with the memory and bandwidth of an HDR canvas buffer.
suggestion: Enable rendering/viewport/hdr_2d explicitly so the project settings match what runs, and budget for the HDR canvas buffer.
expected_effect: Godot uses the configuration as written instead of overriding or ignoring it; no performance saving is asserted.
verify_step: audit_project_rendering or scan_scene, then run the game and confirm the warning is gone from the output
